title: BLiMPPI: Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs for Polarity Items
abstract: arXiv:2610.13607v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Negative polarity items (NPIs), such as "anymore" and "ever", are grammatical only in select environments, predominantly in the context of negation. Because their grammaticality depends on both syntax and semantics, they have a rich, multilingual literature in theoretical linguistics, yet work on NPIs in language models is almost entirely confined to English. We introduce BLiMPPI, a multilingual evaluation suite of over 12,000 NPI minimal pairs in 33 languages, built by a pipeline that discovers NPIs in Universal Dependencies (UD) treebanks, labels their licensing environments, and perturbs these into minimal pairs. Evaluating 12 multilingual and 2 monolingual models alongside n-gram baselines, we find that multilingual models struggle most with lower-resource languages and with pairs that are not n-gram solvable. We further examine the effects of NPI typology, language family, licensing variability, and NPI-licenser distance. Data: http

translated_title: BLiMPPI：极性项语言学最小对立对基准
translated_abstract: 否定极性项（NPI），如"anymore"和"ever"，仅在特定环境中才符合语法，主要出现在否定的语境中。由于其语法性同时取决于句法和语义，它们在理论语言学中拥有丰富的多语言文献，然而语言模型中关于NPI的研究几乎完全局限于英语。我们提出了BLiMPPI，一个涵盖33种语言、包含超过12,000个NPI最小对立对的多语言评估套件。该套件由一个自动化流程构建，该流程在通用依存树库中发现NPI，标注其许可环境，并将其扰动为最小对立对。通过对12个多语言模型和2个单语模型以及n-gram基线进行评估，我们发现多语言模型在低资源语言以及无法通过n-gram方法解决的最小对立对上表现最差。我们进一步检验了NPI类型学、语系、许可变异性以及NPI与许可词之间距离的影响。
tldr: 本文提出了BLiMPPI——一个涵盖33种语言、包含超过12,000个否定极性项最小对立对的多语言评测基准，揭示了多语言模型在低资源语言以及需要深层句法语义知识的NPI现象上表现最差。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces BLiMPPI, a multilingual evaluation suite of over 12,000 NPI minimal pairs across 33 languages, revealing that multilingual language models struggle most with lower-resource languages and with NPI phenomena that require deep syntactic and semantic knowledge.
